page: The Vultr vc2-2c-2gb is an entry-level virtual machine within the Cloud Compute lineup, configured with 2 shared vCPUs across a single physical core on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. System memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB, providing an allocation of 1.0 GB per virtual core. Local storage is provided as a bundled 65 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of shared-core execution and low resource density. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 2453.98 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 2444.49, placing overall compute capability in the lower percentile ranges. Memory throughput tests show 12.18 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 10.85 GB/sec for large writes, with a PassMark memory score of 938.79. In operational benchmarks, the server delivers 1.39 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves 1.72 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Given its shared compute model and low total memory capacity, the vc2-2c-2gb is designed for low-footprint, cost-efficient infrastructure rather than resource-intensive execution. Hardware limitations preclude memory-heavy deployments or complex parallel builds. The server is primarily suitable for lightweight edge services, development environments, small-scale web servers, basic automation jobs, and light proxy tasks.
